Updating the firmware in one or more Dx38 units

Before your Dx38 can transmit or receive data using the RS-485 interface, you need to send an updated version of Dx38 firmware (Version 2.00 or higher) to your devices. This can be done using either RS-232 or RS-485. The RS-232 firmware update is described in the Readme file.

A RS-485 firmware update only works, if your actual firmware version is at least V2.00. If it is not, you must use RS-232 to perform the firmware update. The following paragraph describes the RS-485 firmware update.

To perform it, make all connections and settings as described in the readme file. Then choose Remote > Update Firmware > RS-485 from the menu. RACE will perform a netscan. Now you can see a list of all detected devices with their actual firmware versions. By clicking on appropriate button(s), you can select the device(s) to receive new firmware versions. If there are no detected devices, you can send a new firmware anyway (in that case RACE will try to send a new firmware to all devices connected on RS-485).

You can now browse for the firmware file, which came with RACE. It can be found in the folder RACE/os. Open this file by double-clicking it. The transfer will begin automatically. Note that the displays of the receiving devices will be empty while the file is transferred.  After the firmware is transferred, RACE will perform a new netscan, and you will see results of sending firmware in appropriate dialog-box. In the event of a problem with the firmware update, please refer to the Readme file for further instructions.
